title: Debugging mystery: the certificate that expired in production
intro: Users suddenly get scary 'your connection is not private' warnings. The site was fine yesterday. Find out what broke, and why nobody saw it coming.

start.situation:
$ curl -I https://api.example.com
curl: (60) SSL certificate problem: certificate has expired

The TLS certificate is expired. First move?

choices.label: openssl s_client to read the cert's actual dates

restart.situation:
$ kubectl rollout restart deploy/ingress-nginx -n ingress

The ingress restarts and serves... the same expired certificate. Restarting doesn't mint a new cert, it just reloads the one that's already there, which is expired.
restart.text: Restarting reloads the existing certificate, it doesn't renew it. An expired cert has to be re-issued, not rebooted.

dns.situation:
$ dig +short api.example.com
203.0.113.10

DNS resolves fine to the right IP, and the error was a TLS handshake problem (certificate expired), which happens after the connection is established. This isn't a name-resolution issue.
dns.text: A TLS 'certificate has expired' error happens during the handshake, after DNS already resolved and the TCP connection opened. The name side is fine.

openssl.situation:
$ echo | openssl s_client -connect api.example.com:443 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -dates
notBefore=Jan 15 00:00:00 2026 GMT
notAfter=Apr 15 00:00:00 2026 GMT

Issued in January, expired three days ago. These are 90-day Let's Encrypt certs that are supposed to auto-renew. So the real question is: why didn't renewal happen?

choices.label: It must be a manually-managed cert someone forgot

manual.situation:
$ kubectl get certificate api-tls
NAME      READY   SECRET        AGE
api-tls   False   api-tls-cert  89d

It's not manual, there's a cert-manager Certificate object, and it's been trying to manage this for 89 days. READY is False. cert-manager has been failing to renew it.
manual.text: There IS automation (a cert-manager Certificate). The cert didn't expire because nobody renewed it by hand, it expired because the automated renewal was failing. Find out why.

certmanager.situation:
$ kubectl describe certificate api-tls
...
Status:
  Conditions:
    Ready: False
Events:
  Warning  Failed  Failed to renew: order failed: HTTP-01 challenge failed:
           GET http://api.example.com/.well-known/acme-challenge/xyz -> 404

cert-manager has been trying to renew for weeks, but the ACME HTTP-01 challenge gets a 404. The challenge path isn't reaching cert-manager's solver. What changed?

choices.label: An ingress rule now routes /.well-known/* to the app, not the ACME solver

fix.situation:
Right: a recent ingress change added a catch-all rule that sends every path (including /.well-known/acme-challenge/*) to the app, which 404s it. cert-manager's solver never gets the challenge, so renewal fails silently every cycle until the cert finally expires.

You exclude the ACME challenge path from the catch-all (or use DNS-01 instead). cert-manager completes the order, a fresh cert is issued, and READY goes True.
fix.text: Solved! The cert didn't 'just expire', automated renewal had been failing for weeks because an ingress rule swallowed the ACME HTTP-01 challenge path (404). The expiry was the last visible symptom of a long-broken renewal. The lesson: alert on renewal HEALTH and days-to-expiry (say, < 21 days), not on the cert already being expired, by then it's an outage.
